title: Fargate: containers with no instance to manage

videos.script: Lesson 8 ran a task on an instance you launched, patched and paid for whether it was full or empty. {{instance}} Fargate takes the instance away. You hand ECS the same task definition, and AWS finds the machine. This lesson is about what changes when it does. {{eni}} First the network. Each task gets its own interface in your subnet, its own address, and its own security group. The rules move from the instance to the task. {{price}} Then the bill. You pay for what the task reserves, by the second, and nothing for room nobody uses. You will price a small service on x86 and on Arm, and set it beside the instance from lesson 8. {{spot}} Then Fargate Spot. The same task, cheaper, with two minutes' warning before AWS takes it back. You will watch a container catch the signal and save its work, and watch one that runs out of time. {{giveup}} Last, what goes with the instance. No host to log into, no privileged containers, no daemon on every machine. moto lets all of that through, so you will see exactly where AWS would have said no.
